thread_title: S. rosea 'big mama' x rosea clone C, Mobile Co, AL
breadcrumb: S. rosea 'big mama' x rosea clone C, Mobile Co, AL

posts.body_html:
Sadly, I lost my rosea to big mama a good 2 years ago to rot, but I was able to squeeze out some seeds before she got "aced." The whole point of this big mama cross is to get the fattest of the fat genes displayed while at the same time, the hope was to get some well shaped traps. I did some selecting from the seed batch, and the 3 that were kept were 2-3X the size of the rest of the plants, displayed incredible vigor, and it looks like 2 of the 3 have nice shapes.

S. rosea 'Big mama' x rosea clone C Mobile Co, AL. Photos taken 8/8/15. Here's the clone I have my eye on, which seems to have inherited its shape from clone C:


Another shot of the same clone:

posts.body_html:
Very sad that I lost the original big mama plant, but those tears have long since dried up now that the offspring seem to be even better! The craziest fact about these seedlings is that they were sown on 11/16/13, which makes them a few weeks older than 2 years to this day!

As you can see from the photos taken above, the traps were about average to normal sized in August. I completely neglected and forgot about these plants until one day I walked by and all of the sudden there were these gigantic traps on them. Where did they come from? All of them were produced around late October/November, probably because of the heat wave/indian summer we experienced this year.

Photos of S. rosea 'big mama x rosea clone C Mobile Co, AL taken 12/1/15, these are still "baby" traps compared to how big they can get....and the newest traps on this plant are GIANT:

















This last clone is about regular sized and isn't gigantic like the first two above, but it has a really nice shape. Perhaps it'll get giant later on:

posts.body_html:
OMG - these young plants are stunning and hard to believe they're not yet adult! What an amazing cross this has proved to be. I'm sure all purpurea lovers will be drooling!!

The 2nd clone is my favourite with awesome pitcher form. I love the tubby shape, open large hood, great veination and lovely nectar roll. All this an in a giant form. I can see this cross producing some highly sought after giant rosea/burkii clones. Congratulations Mike and every credit due.

Can't wait to see these beauties develop further as they mature.

posts.body_html:
Hi Flora,

Sorry for the late reply, didn't see your question until now. The female parts were completely fertile as I was able to get seeds, and I don't remember if the male parts ended up shedding pollen or not. This was the first bloom, and they're not always very fertile at this point. I've had a lot of first bloom plants not shed pollen the first year or produce seeds the first year, but the second bloom had no issues.
